A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAP study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, allowing additions, relocations, and retained content to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of GAP models on four visual reasoning datasets, including sample-efficiency experiments, OOD evaluations, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments with Super-CLEVR objects and alternative saliency extractors in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Appendix E adds two optional saliency pipelines: error neurons applied to ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 features, and the Itti et al. saliency extractor. The original GAP procedure, glimpse sensors, and downstream architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds an OOD test set for the existing CLEVR-ART identity-rules task using more realistic Super-CLEVR objects, including cars, planes, and motorbikes. This extends object coverage while retaining the original reasoning task and all previous datasets.

E2.justification: Table E.8 adds CNN+EN and Itti-based IK saliency variants to comparisons on the original CLEVR-ART identity-rules test and the new OOD test. Existing benchmark baseline sets remain unchanged; Slot-Abstractor is reused as the external baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces a comparison of three saliency pipelines, including an ImageNet-pretrained feature-extraction arm, with reasoning-task training on the original cube-only CLEVR-ART set. The previously reported splits, preprocessing, metrics, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E newly tests how saliency extraction affects robustness to more realistic objects, reporting original/OOD accuracy and example saliency maps. Existing input-stream and patch-selection ablations are retained as D.2 and D.3; the new D.1 discusses previously reported sensor comparisons.

E5.justification: Repeated-model counts and uncertainty practices for retained experiments are unchanged. Table E.8 follows the existing CLEVR-ART practice of averaging five trained models and reporting values with ± variability; no new statistical procedure or seed reporting is introduced.

E6.justification: Table E.8 newly reports Super-CLEVR accuracies of 24.1% for Slot-Abstractor, 72.3% for GAP-Abstractor EN, 80.2% for CNN+EN, and 82.1% for IK. It also adds original-test scores of 92.7% and 90.2% for the two new variants. Numerical results in Tables 1–4 and D.1–D.7 are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for glimpse selection, inhibition of return, error neurons, and relational cross-attention remain unchanged, including Appendix A. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about what/where factorization, sample efficiency, OOD generalization, and extensibility. Appendix E supplies additional support for the existing scalability claim.

C2.justification: New Section D.1 explains sensor tradeoffs and why neither sensor consistently dominates. Appendix E interprets alternative saliency extractors' benefits on complex objects alongside lower original-test accuracy. Figure B.3 also suggests subtle shape differences as an explanation for difficult straight-line and rectangle cases.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly states that code is publicly available and supplies a repository link. Appendix E identifies the first layer of an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 as the CNN+EN feature extractor. Appendix C otherwise retains the existing implementation details and hyperparameters.

R1.justification: Section 3 expands discussion of foveal and reinforcement-learning attention, image captioning, AdaGlimpse, and possible connections to visually extended LLMs. Appendix E adds the Super-CLEVR reference. These additions broaden context while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized expansions to related work, task explanations, and discussion, adds a sensor-discussion subsection and Appendix E, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes from a two-row arrangement to a horizontal strip. v2 adds difficult-case Figure B.3, saliency Figure E.8, and Table E.8, relocates retained displays, and corrects Table D.5's second block heading from SD to SR.

improvement.justification: Appendix E provides useful evidence for the previously proposed extension to more complex objects, while D.1 explains sensor tradeoffs and Section 5 adds code-access information. These improve support and usability modestly. The added evaluation remains one synthetic task with incompletely specified test-set construction, and alternative saliency extractors trade some original-test accuracy for stronger OOD performance.
